question.text: Scenario: Arjun Malhotra is analyzing the Indian pharmaceutical industry for a sector report. His PESTLE analysis reveals: Political: Government promoting generic drug manufacturing through production-linked incentive (PLI) schemes. The Jan Aushadhi scheme promotes affordable generic medicines. Economic: India is the world's largest supplier of generic drugs (60% of global supply). The industry exports to 200+ countries with exports worth $27 billion. Pharma is counter-cyclical — demand is inelastic to economic cycles. Socio-cultural: Rising health consciousness, increasing lifestyle diseases (diabetes, cardiovascular), and aging population driving demand. Technological: Digital health, telemedicine, and AI-driven drug discovery are creating new opportunities. Legal: Drug Price Control Order (DPCO) regulates prices of essential medicines. US FDA inspections are critical for export-oriented companies. Patent expiry of major drugs (i.e. the "patent cliff") removes intellectual-property protection and opens the market to Indian generic manufacturers. Environmental: Growing emphasis on green chemistry and sustainable manufacturing. Effluent treatment requirements adding to operating costs. Question 3 of 5: Per the NISM Series XV workbook's definition of Legal factors as "the legal architecture protecting businesses, including intellectual property rights", the patent cliff and resulting loss of IP protection on blockbuster drugs is best classified under which PESTLE category?

answer.text: Legal — as it relates to intellectual property law and the legal architecture protecting businesses
Political — as governments decide on patent policies
Technological — as it relates to technology and innovation cycles in drug development
Socio-cultural — as it reflects societal preferences

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series XV (Research Analyst, Feb 2026), p.119, defines Legal factors as "the legal architecture protecting businesses", which expressly includes intellectual property rights. The patent cliff is the loss of patent (IP) protection on blockbuster drugs as patents expire, which is a legal/IP event. The correct PESTLE classification under the workbook's definition is therefore Legal (option A). The Trap: Option B confuses government policy formation (Political) with the legal IP framework. Option C plays on the surface association between drug development and "Technological", but the workbook's Technological factors are framed as technology support, R&D capability and technology-based initiatives, not patent-protection expiry. Option D is unrelated. In the original ambiguous version the question itself embedded the answer ("Patent cliff creating opportunities for generic manufacturers is classified under:") and keyed Technological, but both Legal/IP and Technological/innovation-cycle interpretations were defensible because the workbook does not discuss patent cliffs directly. Note: The original question was ambiguous because the workbook (p.119) describes Technological and Legal factors broadly and does not discuss patent cliffs explicitly. The stem has been tightened to anchor the answer to the workbook's definition of Legal factors as the legal architecture protecting businesses (including IP rights), and to describe the patent cliff explicitly as a loss of IP protection. The keyed answer has been flipped from Technological to Legal so that option A is uniquely correct under that definition. The "Technological" Patent-cliff sentence has been moved out of the Technological row in the scenario to avoid double-keying. Source: NISM Series XV (Research Analyst, Feb 2026), p.119.
